sentence.en: Websites, custom software and automation, engineered to last.

set.name: Layered E
set.mechanism: An isometric E folded from three slabs, stepping cyan to blue to violet: a system built in layers. Every edge sits on the 30-degree isometric grid, with one gap between all slabs.
set.expression_move: The three-step colour ramp across the slabs; everything else is midnight, navy and ice white.
set.differs_by: Software-studio marks are mostly flat glyphs or arrows; the isometric fold gives depth with flat colour, and the IT in cyan says what the company does.

logo.concept: The client's layered E, regularised on an isometric lattice: three slabs, one gap, two equal fold notches.

misuse.label: Do not close the gaps between the slabs
Do not reverse the colour order

defaults_used.why: Client palette and client mark: violet is the last step of the mark's ramp, never a UI primary.
Client palette: Midnight and Navy are grounds; Cyan is the identifying colour.

rationale.claim: Mark refined from the client's own kit (Nov 2026): same silhouette, rebuilt on a true isometric lattice with one gap (2 units) and equal fold notches (1.5 units). The original had gaps from 0.5 to 2 units.
rationale.source: contour extraction of the client's one-colour logo

rationale.claim: Lexend's slab-serifed capital I keeps ElIT from reading as EIIT in one colour; the client kit's wordmark read EIIT.
Lexend is the logo face only (outlined, Latin letters); Geologica covers Greek and tabular figures for all running text.
